page_hint: Chapter 7 (Memory Is the First Constraint), Table 7-1 fit/non-fit rows + the 'does it fit?' note (printed-page offset unconfirmed — only the manuscript chunk was supplied, no locked PDF)
quoted_clause: 8×H100 (no sharding ambiguity at 8 shards) passes gates 1–2 for the 9.2K and 32K rows; the 3×H100 row and the 128K row pass gate 1 only ... fits 8×H100 at 128K? | passes aggregate bytes only; runtime config not established ... 475.5 GB < 640 GB
observed: The note groups the 128K-on-8×H100 row with the 3×H100 row as 'pass gate 1 only', implying both fail gate 2 (per-rank/shard compatibility). The 3×H100 failure is a genuine sharding issue (8192/3 is non-integral). But 128K on 8×H100 uses TP=8, for which 8192/8 = 1024 is integral — the same sharding the note says PASSES gate 2 for the 32K row. Context length changes KV size, not hidden-dim sharding, so the stated gate-2 rationale does not transfer from 3×H100 to 128K. The 128K row's own cell attributes the caveat to 'runtime config not established' (a gate-3 / working-benchmark concern), not gate 2.
evidence: 8192/8 = 1024 (integral) ⇒ TP=8 sharding viable at any context incl. 128K; 8192/3 = 2730.67 (non-integral) ⇒ TP=3 sharding fails for the 3×H100 row. The 32K and 128K rows are both 8×H100/TP=8 and therefore share gate-2 sharding status, yet the note assigns them different gate-2 verdicts. Recomputed 128K residency = 140 + 335.5 = 475.5 GB < 640 GB (aggregate passes); per-rank under TP=8 ≈ 17.5 GB weights + ~42 GB KV ≈ 59.5 GB/GPU — a per-rank workspace / long-context-runtime question (gate-2 workspace sub-clause or gate 3), not a hidden-dim sharding failure. Benign reading available: gate 2's own definition includes 'runtime/workspace ... must be supported', and 128K workspace >> 32K workspace, so the note MAY be leaning on that sub-clause — which is exactly why the grouping should be made explicit rather than conflated with the 3×H100 sharding failure.
root_cause: Gate-attribution imprecision in the supporting note: it conflates a true sharding failure (3×H100, 8192/3 non-integral) with a long-context runtime/workspace caveat (128K on TP=8), assigning both 'gate 1 only'. The row-level text (gate 3 / runtime config) and the note (gate 2 also fails) disagree on which gate bounds the 128K case.
correction: State that 128K on 8×H100 passes gates 1–2 (TP=8 sharding of hidden-dim 8192 is integral) and lacks only gate 3 (long-context runtime/workspace benchmark) — matching the 32K treatment and the row's own 'runtime config not established' text — OR explicitly tie the 128K caveat to gate 2's 'runtime/workspace' sub-clause and show the per-rank 128K budget. Do not group it with the 3×H100 sharding failure.
acceptance_test: Re-derive the gate-2 verdict for the 128K-on-8×H100 row: confirm 8192/8 = 1024 is integral (TP=8 sharding viable) and decide whether the 128K caveat is gate 2 (per-rank workspace at 128K) or gate 3 (runtime benchmark). Align the note's grouping with the row-level text so both name the same bounding gate.

page_hint: Chapter 8 end-of-chapter mini-case (Continuous Deployment Scenario). Exact PDF/printed page not determinable from the provided chunk; locate at the Ch8 mini-case and cross-check Table 8-1.
quoted_clause: ~10 requests/s average with ~9.2K input + 300 output tokens per request ... on 8×H100 GPUs, with prefill ~1.29 PFLOP per request (2 ×70B × L tokens; Table 8-1)
observed: Sustained prefill compute demand at the stated operating point = 10 req/s × (2 × 70e9 × 9,200) FLOP/req = 10 × 1.288e15 = 1.29e16 FLOP/s ≈ 12.9 PFLOP/s. 8×H100 FP16 dense peak = 8 × 989 TFLOPS = 7.91 PFLOP/s (house convention: 989 dense). Demand = 163% of dense peak, so a DENSE 70B model cannot sustain ~10 req/s of 9.2K-token prefills on 8×H100 even at 100% MFU. The scenario asserts BOTH that it is serving ~10 req/s AND that it runs on 8×H100; those are jointly feasible only if the model is MoE (active ≲ 30B), 2:4 sparsity is assumed (peak → 15.8 PFLOP/s, ~81% MFU), or the true average input length is well below 9.2K.
evidence: Recomputed from the book's own formula (2×70B×L, with 9.2K = 9,200 per house convention) and the stated fleet (8×H100, 989 dense). 2×70e9×9,200 = 1.288e15 = ~1.29 PFLOP/req (matches the printed Table 8-1 value); ×10 req/s = 1.29e16 = 12.9 PFLOP/s; 8×989e12 = 7.91e15 = 7.91 PFLOP/s; 12.9/7.91 = 1.63. MoE escape: 16B-active → 2.94 PFLOP/s (37% peak); 37B-active → 6.81 PFLOP/s (86% peak).
root_cause: Possible fixed-fleet-vs-workload operating-point mismatch (throughput conservation): stated req/s × per-request prefill FLOP exceeds the stated fleet's peak FP16 capacity. May be benign if the '70B-class' model is MoE (fewer active params), if sparsity is assumed, or if 8×H100 is not the full prefill tier (the case itself recommends P/D disaggregation).
correction: State the model's active parameter count (dense vs MoE) and whether sparsity applies. If dense-70B on exactly 8×H100, reconcile by adding a prefill/disaggregated tier, lowering the stated req/s, or reducing the canonical input length used for the sustained-throughput claim.
acceptance_test: Compute fleet peak FP16 capacity (8 × 989 TFLOPS = 7.91 PFLOP/s dense; ×2 with 2:4 sparsity) and sustained prefill demand (req/s × 2 × active_params × 9,200). Require demand ≤ capacity at a plausible MFU (30–40%); if violated for dense-70B on 8×H100, correct the scenario inputs or fleet size. A different-model re-derivation from the quoted text is required to confirm/dispute (single-model pass cannot self-certify P1).
